brief:
## (a) Browser sign-in earlier: JS-215 moves up, password only, before the cutover

- decision: `change`. JS-215 no longer waits for the cutover (JS-194) or for single sign-on. It follows JS-184 and runs beside JS-216's remainder.
- serves: PRODUCT.md, "Signing in is easy and safe"; Goal 3.
- reason: browser viewers sign in through Octave Web. Its sign-in is the one #301 makes safe, and nothing in it needs Jellyfin's routes to have gone. It does need three things:
  - JS-184's accounts and devices on v1;
  - a server Octave can start (JS-198);
  - a page on the server's own site, because a sign-in that other sites can't use can't work from another origin either.

  Today's `webDir` lets an operator, or Octave's CI, serve an Octave Web build from the server itself. JS-150 (the shipped release) still waits on its own dependencies.
- What it must not wait for: JS-039 (single sign-on), JS-194 and JS-150.
- What it must not break before the cutover: Jellyfin's routes never read the web sign-in, and they keep invariant 63 (no cookie, any origin), so jellyfin-web plays as before.
- JS-215 amended:
  - dependsOn: JS-184 and JS-223 (was JS-184 and JS-194).
  - Criterion 1: "A browser signs in by password and holds no credential its page's scripts can read." Single sign-on's part moves to JS-039, whose note (#296) already covers it.
  - Added: "Until the cutover the web sign-in is read only on `/jellyscale/v1/` and its picture route. No Jellyfin route reads it or sets a cookie, so invariant 63 holds for them unchanged and jellyfin-web plays as before."
  - Added: "A page served by the server's `webDir` signs in by password, reloads still signed in, reads `/me`, and signs out, in the e2e tier with real processes. A page on another origin cannot use the sign-in."
- JS-150: unchanged, except that it no longer waits for JS-215's position (it still depends on JS-215).
- Order: JS-223, JS-184, JS-198, **JS-215**, JS-216, … JS-215 may run beside JS-216's remainder and beside JS-198.
- Ask of Octave: "Test Octave Web's sign-in from a build served by the server's `webDir` (same site). A build on another origin will not keep the sign-in, by design. Tell us whether that fits your test setup before JS-215's Spec."
- entry: "Browser sign-in (JS-215) moves up to follow JS-184, password only, before the cutover. It is read only on jellyscale's own API, and Jellyfin's routes keep invariant 63. Single sign-on's web part moves to JS-039. Octave tests it from a build served by the server's webDir."
tradeoff: A build on another origin will not keep the sign-in, by design.
serves: PRODUCT.md, "Signing in is easy and safe"; Goal 3.
